sentences.text: Torosteus had a body shape and size similar to Incisoscutum and Compagopiscis, implying it likely lived in open water.
Remains of this ancient fish have been discovered in the Kimberley region of Australia.
Scientists analyzing bite force suggest Torosteus was an active predator.
The large number of fossils found suggests the possibility of schooling behavior.
Torosteus is currently classified as a member of the superfamily Incisoscutoidea within the clade Coccosteomorphi.
This extinct arthrodire placoderm — a type of armored fish — lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago during the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
